experiences.name: Annapurna Base Camp Trek
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic multi-day trek to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, passing through rhododendron forests, terraced fields, and traditional Gurung villages. Witness breathtaking panoramic views of Annapurna I, Machapuchare, and Hiunchuli peaks. The trail offers diverse landscapes from subtropical jungle to alpine terrain, making it one of the world's most rewarding trekking experiences.

experiences.name: Poon Hill Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike to Poon Hill viewpoint at 3,210m for one of the most spectacular sunrises in the Himalayas. Watch golden light illuminate the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges while clouds drift through the valleys below. The 2-hour ascent from Ghorepani is manageable for most fitness levels and rewards trekkers with a 180-degree panorama of over a dozen peaks above 7,000m.

experiences.name: Gurung Village Cultural Homestay in Ghandruk
experiences.description: Spend a night or two in the traditional Gurung village of Ghandruk, staying with a local family in an authentic stone-and-timber home. Learn about Gurung culture, traditions, and cuisine while enjoying homemade dal bhat, millet raksi, and local vegetables. Explore the village's narrow cobblestone lanes, visit the Gurung Museum, and interact with locals who have maintained their ancestral way of life for centuries.

experiences.name: Modi Khola River Valley Nature Walk
experiences.description: Explore the lush Modi Khola river valley on a guided nature walk through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests teeming with wildlife. Spot Himalayan tahr, langur monkeys, and over 100 bird species including the vibrant Danphe pheasant, Nepal's national bird. A knowledgeable local naturalist guide will identify medicinal plants, explain the unique ecosystem of the Annapurna Conservation Area, and share insights into the region's biodiversity.
experiences.location: Modi Khola Valley, Annapurna Conservation Area

experiences.name: Thorong La High Pass Crossing
experiences.description: Challenge yourself with the legendary crossing of Thorong La Pass at 5,416m, the highest point on the Annapurna Circuit and one of the highest trekking passes in the world. Starting from Thorong Phedi in the pre-dawn darkness, the 7-8 hour ascent and descent to Muktinath is physically demanding but enormously rewarding. The pass offers surreal views of the Tibetan plateau, Kali Gandaki gorge, and the towering peaks of the Annapurna and Mustang regions.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Annapurna, Nepal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Clear immigration, collect luggage, and exchange currency at the airport. Take a budget tourist bus or shared taxi to Thamel (Kathmandu's backpacker hub). Check into a budget guesthouse for one night. Walk around Thamel to pick up any last-minute trekking gear, snacks, and a SIM card (Ncell or NTC). Visit a local gear shop to rent trekking poles or sleeping bag liner if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Thamel's lively streets. Visit a rooftop restaurant for a classic Nepali Dal Bhat dinner. Organize your pack for the early bus departure tomorrow. Rest and acclimatize.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the airport or a local tea shop near Thamel (~NPR 200–300)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at a local Thamel restaurant such as OR2K or New Everest Steak House (~NPR 400–600)

day_by_day.notes: Book your Pokhara bus ticket tonight for Day 2 morning. Obtain your TIMS card and ACAP permit in Kathmandu or Pokhara (ACAP ~NPR 3,000 for foreigners, TIMS ~NPR 2,000). Keep all documents ready.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 06:00. Take a tourist bus from Kathmandu to Pokhara (departs ~07:00–08:00, ~7–8 hours, costs ~NPR 700–1,000). Enjoy scenic mountain views along the Prithvi Highway. Pack snacks and water for the journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Pokhara around 14:00–15:00. Check into a lakeside budget guesthouse near Phewa Lake. Freshen up and take a relaxed walk along the Lakeside (Baidam) promenade. Browse local shops for any final trekking supplies.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset over Phewa Lake and the Annapurna range from the lakeside. Dinner at a budget lakeside restaurant. Plan tomorrow's journey to the trek starting point (Nayapul or Jhinu Danda). Confirm jeep or bus departure.

meals.breakfast: Bread, eggs, and tea at Thamel guesthouse (~NPR 200–300)
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or roadside dhaba meal en route (~NPR 200–400)
meals.dinner: Momos and thukpa at a lakeside eatery (~NPR 350–500)

day_by_day.notes: Obtain TIMS and ACAP permits at the Nepal Tourism Board office in Pokhara if not already done. Lakeside area has several budget guesthouses for ~NPR 500–800/night.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara by local bus or shared jeep to Nayapul (~1.5 hours, ~NPR 200–300). Begin the trek from Nayapul (1,070m). Trek through Modi Khola valley passing Birethanti. Enjoy lush subtropical forests, terraced fields, and river views. Reach Hile or Tikhedhunga for a tea break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking uphill through stone-paved steps to Ulleri (1,960m). This section involves a steep climb of approximately 3,000 stone steps — a classic Annapurna challenge. Arrive at Ulleri and check into a teahouse. Rest and enjoy panoramic Annapurna foothills views.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small village of Ulleri. Chat with fellow trekkers on the teahouse porch. Enjoy a warm dinner and early bedtime to prepare for tomorrow's long day.

meals.breakfast: Porridge or eggs at Pokhara guesthouse (~NPR 250)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a Tikhedhunga teahouse (~NPR 400–500)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 500–600)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today: ~10 km, ~5–6 hours. Elevation gain is significant. Stay hydrated. Teahouse accommodation in Ulleri costs ~NPR 300–500/night (often free or discounted if you eat meals there).

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Ulleri. Trek through oak and rhododendron forests to Banthanti (2,250m) and then Nayathanti. October skies should offer clear Annapurna South and Hiunchuli views. Enjoy the cool forest air and birdsong.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking to Ghorepani (2,860m). Arrive by early afternoon. Check into a teahouse. Rest and acclimatize. Visit the village to see traditional Gurung and Magar stone houses. Optional: short acclimatization walk around the village.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the alpenglow on Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, and Nilgiri from the village viewpoint. Warm up with butter tea or hot lemon in the teahouse. Dinner and early sleep — a 04:00 wake-up awaits tomorrow for Poon Hill sunrise.

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or porridge at Ulleri teahouse (~NPR 300)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and chapati at Banthanti teahouse (~NPR 400)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Ghorepani teahouse (~NPR 550–650)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~9 km, ~4–5 hours. Ghorepani has many teahouses — negotiate a good rate. Ask teahouse owner to prepare a packed snack for the Poon Hill sunrise hike tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 04:00. Hike by headlamp to Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m) — about 45 minutes uphill. Watch one of Nepal's most spectacular sunrises over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Enjoy 360-degree panoramic views including Annapurna I, II, III, IV, South, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Dhaulagiri, and Nilgiri. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Ghorepani and trek via Deurali toward Tadapani (2,630m). The trail passes through dense rhododendron and magnolia forests — stunning in October light. Arrive at Tadapani by early afternoon and check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy views of Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South from Tadapani. Relax tired muscles with a warm wash (bucket shower available at most teahouses). Dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and tea after returning from Poon Hill (~NPR 300–400)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or fried rice at Deurali teahouse (~NPR 400)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 500–600)

day_by_day.notes: Poon Hill entry fee: NPR 100. Trek distance today (including Poon Hill): ~12 km, ~6 hours total. Tadapani has fewer teahouses than Ghorepani — arrive early to secure a room.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani to Chomrong (2,170m) via Gurjung. Descend through forest and terraced fields with continuous Machhapuchhre and Annapurna South views. Cross suspension bridges over the Modi Khola. Chomrong is a beautiful Gurung village with stone-paved streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Chomrong by early afternoon. Check into a teahouse with a view. Explore the village — visit the Chomrong Khola area and the small local shops. This is the last major village before entering the Annapurna Sanctuary. Stock up on snacks, water purification tablets, and extra warm layers.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the stunning sunset view of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from Chomrong. Hot shower available at some teahouses (~NPR 200 extra). Dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and honey at Tadapani teahouse (~NPR 300)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at a Gurjung or mid-trail teahouse (~NPR 500)
meals.dinner: Garlic soup, spring rolls, and tea at Chomrong teahouse (~NPR 500–650)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~10 km, ~5 hours. Chomrong has a checkpoint — have your ACAP permit and TIMS card ready. Buy extra chocolate bars and energy snacks here as prices increase significantly higher up.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Chomrong early. Descend stone steps to Chomrong Khola then climb to Sinuwa (2,360m). Trek through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Kuldi and then Bamboo (2,310m). The forest is dense and atmospheric — watch for Himalayan monals and other wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking from Bamboo upward to Dovan (2,600m) and then to Himalaya Hotel (2,900m). The trail follows the Modi Khola gorge with towering canyon walls. Arrive at Himalaya Hotel teahouse and check in. The air is noticeably cooler and thinner.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and acclimatize at Himalaya Hotel. The gorge is dramatic and views are limited here, but the sense of entering the Sanctuary is palpable. Warm up with hot drinks. Dinner and early sleep — the highest point of the trek is two days away.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and chapati at Chomrong teahouse (~NPR 350)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 500)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Himalaya Hotel teahouse (~NPR 600–700)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~12 km, ~6–7 hours. Prices increase significantly from here. Dal Bhat may cost NPR 700–900 in the Sanctuary. Carry a water bottle and use purification tablets — stream water is generally safe but treat it. Beware of leeches in the forest sections.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Himalaya Hotel to Deurali (3,230m). The trail becomes more exposed and rocky. Pass through avalanche zones — move steadily and avoid stopping in open gully areas. Views of the Sanctuary walls begin to emerge. Arrive at Deurali for a tea break.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the dramatic final push into the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) bowl. Pass Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) — a good lunch stop with stunning Fishtail Mountain views. Continue upward to Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m). Arrive at the Boutique Stay / teahouse accommodation in the Annapurna Sanctuary. Check in and rest immediately.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the golden hour light paint Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Gangapurna, and Glacier Dome. The 360-degree amphitheater of Himalayan giants is extraordinary. Hot drinks and acclimatization rest. Dinner in the teahouse dining hall with fellow trekkers.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Himalaya Hotel (~NPR 400)
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and fried noodles at MBC (~NPR 600–700)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at ABC teahouse (~NPR 800–1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~10 km, ~5–6 hours. This is the highest point of the trek at 4,130m. Watch for signs of altitude sickness: headache, nausea, dizziness. Drink plenty of water. Do NOT ascend if feeling severely unwell — descend immediately. October weather is generally stable but temperatures drop to -5°C to -10°C at night.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn to watch the sunrise from ABC. The spectacle of first light hitting the Annapurna massif is one of the most breathtaking sights in the Himalayas. Take a guided exploration walk around the base camp area, approaching the glacier moraine for close-up views of the icefall and seracs. Photography and quiet contemplation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring the Annapurna Sanctuary bowl. Walk toward the South Annapurna Glacier viewpoint. Observe the dramatic scale of the surrounding peaks. Rest, journal, and acclimatize. Optional: short hike to a higher vantage point near the camp for broader panoramas.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening at ABC. Watch the alpenglow on the peaks at dusk. Share stories with other trekkers in the teahouse. Warm dinner and prepare gear for descent tomorrow. Sleep early.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal, boiled eggs, and hot lemon at ABC teahouse (~NPR 500)
meals.lunch: Fried rice or pasta at ABC teahouse (~NPR 700)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat and vegetable curry at ABC teahouse (~NPR 900)

day_by_day.notes: Rest day at ABC for acclimatization and full appreciation of the Sanctuary. Stay warm — temperatures remain very cold. Avoid overexertion. Carry a daypack with water, snacks, and a first aid kit for any walks. This is the highlight of the entire trek.

day_by_day.morning: Begin descent from ABC (4,130m) back down to MBC and continue to Bamboo (2,310m). Descent is faster but hard on the knees — use trekking poles. The valley and forest views feel lush after days at altitude. Pass through Deurali and Himalaya Hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending through bamboo forest to Bamboo teahouse. Check in and rest. The warmer, thicker air at lower altitude feels noticeably refreshing. Wash up with a bucket shower.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Bamboo teahouse. Enjoy a hearty meal — appetite often returns strongly after descending from altitude. Chat with upward-bound trekkers and share trail conditions. Early rest.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at ABC teahouse (~NPR 500)
meals.lunch: Noodle soup at Himalaya Hotel or Dovan (~NPR 500)
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 600)

day_by_day.notes: Descent distance: ~14 km, ~5–6 hours. Knees take significant strain on descent — pace yourself and use poles. Watch footing on wet or rocky sections. Bamboo area can be misty in the evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Bamboo back to Chomrong via Sinuwa. The climb back up to Chomrong involves a steep ascent — take it slow. Enjoy the familiar forest trail and expanding mountain views as you gain elevation. Arrive at Chomrong by mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Chomrong, take the alternative trail toward Jhinu Danda (1,780m) — a beautiful descent through terraced fields and forest. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs on the banks of the Modi Khola. Arrive by afternoon and check into a teahouse.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda (~NPR 200–300 entry) — a perfect reward for tired muscles after 9 days of trekking. The setting beside the rushing river is magical. Return to the teahouse for dinner and a well-earned rest.

meals.breakfast: Porridge and tea at Bamboo teahouse (~NPR 350)
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat at Chomrong teahouse (~NPR 550)
meals.dinner: Vegetable curry and rice at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~NPR 500–600)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~11 km, ~5 hours. The hot springs are open until around 18:00 — arrive before dark. Jhinu Danda is a quieter, more peaceful stop than Chomrong. Enjoy the sound of the river at night.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda down to Siwai and then to Nayapul (1,070m) via the Modi Khola valley. The trail follows the river through beautiful subtropical scenery — a fitting farewell to the Annapurna foothills. Pass through Birethanti and reach Nayapul by late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or shared jeep from Nayapul back to Pokhara (~1.5 hours, ~NPR 200–300). Arrive in Pokhara and check into a Lakeside budget guesthouse. Celebrate completing the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek! Take a refreshing proper shower and do laundry.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate at a Lakeside restaurant with a well-deserved special meal. Enjoy a cold Everest beer or a fresh fruit lassi. Stroll along Phewa Lake at dusk. Reflect on the trek over dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eggs and chapati at Jhinu Danda teahouse (~NPR 300)
meals.lunch: Quick snack at Birethanti or packed food (~NPR 300)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner — Nepali thali or grilled fish at a Lakeside restaurant (~NPR 600–800)

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance: ~9 km to Nayapul, ~4 hours. You have completed the full Annapurna Sanctuary circuit — approximately 110 km over 10 trekking days. Well done! Rest your legs tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Pokhara. Sleep in. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at a Lakeside café. Optional: rent a rowboat on Phewa Lake (~NPR 400–600/hour) and paddle to Tal Barahi Temple on the island in the middle of the lake. Enjoy peaceful lake and mountain reflections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the World Peace Pagoda (Shanti Stupa) on the southern hill above Phewa Lake — hike up (~1.5 hours) or take a short boat ride and climb for free. Panoramic views of Pokhara, Phewa Lake, and the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges. Explore the Pokhara Museum or the International Mountain Museum (~NPR 300 entry) to learn about Himalayan mountaineering history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lakeside's restaurants and cafés. Enjoy a sunset lakeside dinner. Browse souvenir shops for gifts — pashmina scarves, Thangka paintings, and handmade paper products are good budget-friendly options. Early rest before the return journey tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancakes and coffee at a Lakeside café (~NPR 350)
meals.lunch: Fresh salad and sandwich at a Lakeside café (~NPR 400)
meals.dinner: Buff (buffalo) steak or mixed grill at a budget Lakeside restaurant (~NPR 600–800)

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is a perfect recovery city. Book your Kathmandu bus or flight for Day 14 morning. Tourist bus: ~NPR 700–1,000. Domestic flight (Buddha Air/Yeti Airlines): ~NPR 5,000–8,000 — worth it if budget allows for the spectacular mountain views from the air.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara for Kathmandu by tourist bus (07:00 departure, ~7–8 hours) or domestic flight (30 minutes, stunning Himalayan aerial views). Arrive in Kathmandu by early afternoon. Check into a Thamel guesthouse for the final night.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Visit Boudhanath Stupa — the largest Buddhist stupa in Nepal, a peaceful and atmospheric site. Walk to Pashupatinath Temple (Hindu temple complex on the Bagmati River — exterior viewing free for non-Hindus). Browse Thamel for final souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Kathmandu — splurge slightly on a traditional Newari feast or a rooftop restaurant with Himalayan views. Reflect on an incredible 14-day budget adventure through the Annapurna region. Pack and prepare for departure. Confirm airport transfer for the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Lakeside café breakfast before departure (~NPR 350)
meals.lunch: Roadside dhaba meal en route or airport snack (~NPR 300–500)
meals.dinner: Newari thali or Dal Bhat at a Thamel restaurant (~NPR 500–700)

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary estimate (excluding flights): Permits (ACAP + TIMS): ~NPR 5,000 | Accommodation (13 nights avg NPR 500): ~NPR 6,500 | Meals (avg NPR 600/day x 14): ~NPR 8,400 | Transport: ~NPR 3,000 | Misc/entry fees: ~NPR 2,000. Total estimated: ~NPR 24,900 (~USD 185–200). The Annapurna Sanctuary Trek is one of the world's great trekking experiences — congratulations on completing it on a budget!

trip_options.title: Classic Annapurna, Nepal Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — clear immigration and collect luggage
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Pokhara via tourist bus or shared jeep (approximately 6–7 hours) or take a 25-minute domestic flight to Pokhara if available. Check in to your guesthouse in Pokhara lakeside area and freshen up. Take a short evening stroll along Phewa Lake to acclimatize and orient yourself
day_by_day.evening: Explore Lakeside Bazaar, browse trekking gear shops to confirm equipment, and enjoy a relaxed dinner overlooking Phewa Lake

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a quick bite at Kathmandu airport café
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or momos at a local roadside dhaba en route to Pokhara
meals.dinner: Dinner at Moondance Restaurant or similar lakeside mid-range restaurant in Pokhara — try Nepali thali or grilled fish from the lake

day_by_day.notes: Do not schedule anything strenuous today. Focus on rest and hydration. Confirm trekking permits (TIMS card and ACAP permit) at the Pokhara tourism office first thing tomorrow morning. Exchange currency if needed at Lakeside.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) office and Nepal Tourism Board to obtain your TIMS card and Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP). Then visit Pokhara's World Peace Pagoda for panoramic views of the Annapurna range and Phewa Lake
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short rowboat ride on Phewa Lake to the Tal Barahi Temple on the island. Afterward, visit the International Mountain Museum in Pokhara to understand the Annapurna massif, its ecology, and trekking history — excellent preparation for the days ahead
day_by_day.evening: Pack your trekking bag carefully, laying out gear for the trek. Enjoy a leisurely dinner and an early night to prepare for the trek start tomorrow

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and fresh juice at your guesthouse or a café on Lakeside Road
meals.lunch: Set lunch at a local Nepali restaurant near the museum — try vegetable curry with rice
meals.dinner: Dinner at Beam Bar & Restaurant or similar — pasta, pizza, or Nepali thali; budget NPR 800–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Permits are mandatory and must be obtained before entering the conservation area. Costs: TIMS ~USD 20, ACAP ~USD 30. Confirm your trek route with your guide or guesthouse — the classic Annapurna Sanctuary (Base Camp) route is recommended for 14 days.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Pokhara by local bus or jeep to Nayapul (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Begin trekking from Nayapul through Birethanti, crossing the Modi Khola suspension bridge and following the river upstream through terraced fields and rhododendron forests toward Tikhedhunga
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through Ulleri, climbing the famous stone staircase of approximately 3,000 steps — a challenging but rewarding ascent through traditional Magar villages. Arrive at Ghorepani or stop at Ulleri for the night depending on pace
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Ulleri or Banthanti teahouse, settle in, and enjoy the cool mountain air. Socialize with fellow trekkers over hot tea

meals.breakfast: Porridge, eggs, and tea at your Pokhara guesthouse before departure
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at a teahouse in Tikhedhunga
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat set meal at Ulleri teahouse — the classic trekker's fuel; NPR 500–700

day_by_day.notes: Today's trek: Nayapul to Ulleri, approximately 9 km, 4–5 hours, elevation gain ~1,960m to ~2,070m. Pace yourself on the stone staircase. Drink plenty of water. October is peak season — teahouses are busy so arrive by 3–4 PM to secure a room.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn and hike from Ulleri (or Banthanti) through dense rhododendron and oak forests to Ghorepani (2,860m). The trail is moderate with beautiful forest scenery. Arrive at Ghorepani by mid-morning and drop your pack at the teahouse
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up to Poon Hill (3,210m) — about 45 minutes from Ghorepani. Enjoy sweeping panoramic views of Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and the surrounding peaks. Note: Many trekkers do this at sunrise the next day, so afternoon visit avoids crowds
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ghorepani for the evening. Warm up by the teahouse fire, meet fellow trekkers, and enjoy the mountain atmosphere

meals.breakfast: Pancakes and honey with tea or coffee at Ulleri teahouse
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and vegetable fried rice at a Ghorepani teahouse
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at your Ghorepani teahouse — NPR 600–900

day_by_day.notes: Ulleri to Ghorepani: approximately 8 km, 3–4 hours. Altitude increases to 2,860m — watch for early signs of altitude sickness (headache, nausea). Drink 3–4 liters of water today. Set an alarm for tomorrow's sunrise hike to Poon Hill (4:30 AM departure recommended).

day_by_day.morning: Rise at 4:30 AM and hike to Poon Hill (3,210m) by headlamp for a spectacular sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges — one of the most iconic views in Nepal. Return to Ghorepani for breakfast, then continue trekking to Tadapani through magnificent rhododendron forests
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Tadapani (2,630m) by early afternoon. Enjoy views of Annapurna South and Hiunchuli from the village. Rest and explore the small settlement. Optional: short walk to a nearby viewpoint above Tadapani
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your teahouse, enjoy the quieter atmosphere of Tadapani compared to Ghorepani, and rest well for tomorrow's longer stage

meals.breakfast: Eggs, toast, and hot lemon tea after returning from Poon Hill
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or tuna sandwich at a teahouse en route to Tadapani
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat with spinach and lentils at Tadapani teahouse — NPR 550–750

day_by_day.notes: Ghorepani to Tadapani: approximately 10 km, 4–5 hours. The rhododendron forest section between Deurali and Tadapani is stunning even in October. Trail can be muddy — trekking poles recommended. Tadapani has fewer teahouses so arrive early.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Tadapani down through terraced farmland and forest to Chhomrong (2,170m), the last major permanent village before the Annapurna Sanctuary. The descent offers beautiful views of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre. Cross the Chhomrong Khola river and climb the stone steps up into the village
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Chhomrong and explore this charming Gurung village. Visit the ACAP checkpoint to have permits stamped. Take a short walk to the upper village for views of Annapurna South towering directly above. Rest and recover from the day's trek
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the vibrant teahouse scene in Chhomrong — it is a hub for trekkers heading in and out of the Sanctuary. Hot shower available at most guesthouses here (last reliable hot shower for several days)

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread with jam and butter and masala tea at Tadapani
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and vegetable momos at a teahouse in Sinuwa or en route
meals.dinner: Apple pie and dal bhat at one of Chhomrong's well-known teahouses such as Chhomrong Cottage — NPR 700–1,000

day_by_day.notes: Tadapani to Chhomrong: approximately 10 km, 4–5 hours. The stone staircase into Chhomrong is steep and tiring at the end of a long day — take it slowly. Chhomrong is the last place to stock up on snacks, chocolate, and supplies before the upper Sanctuary. Prices increase significantly above here.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong descending to Chhomrong Khola then ascending steeply through bamboo and rhododendron forest to Sinuwa (2,360m) and onward to Bamboo (2,310m). The trail enters the increasingly dramatic Modi Khola gorge
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Bamboo through dense bamboo groves and forest to Dovan (2,600m). The gorge narrows and the trail becomes more rugged. Arrive at Dovan teahouses and settle in — the accommodation is more basic here but comfortable enough
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the dramatic gorge setting with the roar of the Modi Khola river. The forest is alive with bird calls. Rest is essential as altitude begins to increase more rapidly from here

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at Chhomrong teahouse
meals.lunch: Instant noodles or dal bhat at Bamboo teahouse
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat or pasta at Dovan teahouse — NPR 700–900 (prices rise inside the Sanctuary)

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong to Dovan: approximately 10 km, 4–5 hours. No alcohol or meat products are allowed beyond Chhomrong inside the Annapurna Sanctuary — this is an ACAP regulation. Teahouses become more basic but remain clean and functional. Watch for leeches on the trail in the bamboo sections even in October.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Dovan through the narrowing gorge past Himalaya Hotel (2,920m) and Hinku Cave (3,170m). The landscape transforms dramatically as the valley opens up. Pass through Deurali (3,230m) — the narrowest and most avalanche-prone section of the route. Move through this section briskly in clear weather
day_by_day.afternoon: Emerge from the gorge into the stunning Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) approach. The Sanctuary opens up with a breathtaking 360-degree amphitheater of Himalayan peaks. Arrive at Machhapuchhre Base Camp (MBC, 3,700m) and check in. Rest and acclimatize — do not rush to ABC today
day_by_day.evening: Watch the alpenglow on Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Peak, 6,993m) — one of the most sacred and unclimbed peaks in Nepal. The evening light on the peaks is extraordinary. Rest well for the big day tomorrow

meals.breakfast: Porridge and hot lemon tea at Dovan
meals.lunch: Garlic soup (excellent for altitude) and crackers at Himalaya Hotel teahouse
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat and vegetable curry at MBC teahouse — NPR 900–1,200

day_by_day.notes: Dovan to MBC: approximately 11 km, 5–6 hours, significant altitude gain to 3,700m. Altitude sickness risk increases here — watch for persistent headache, loss of appetite, dizziness, or nausea. If symptoms are severe, descend immediately. Drink 4+ liters of water. Garlic soup is a local remedy for altitude. MBC teahouses are basic but adequate.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and trek the final 1.5–2 hours from MBC to Annapurna Base Camp (ABC, 4,130m). Arrive at ABC for sunrise — the full 360-degree panorama of Annapurna I (8,091m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, Glacier Dome, Tent Peak, and Machhapuchhre is utterly overwhelming and magnificent
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the morning and early afternoon at ABC exploring the glacier moraine, photographing the peaks, and absorbing the atmosphere of this extraordinary high-altitude sanctuary. Have lunch at the ABC teahouse. Begin descent back toward MBC in the afternoon — it is not advisable to spend the night at ABC unless fully acclimatized
day_by_day.evening: Return to MBC or descend further to Deurali or Himalaya Hotel depending on energy levels. Celebrate reaching Annapurna Base Camp with your trekking companions over dinner

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast of biscuits and hot tea at MBC before the summit push
meals.lunch: Dal Bhat or noodle soup at ABC teahouse — the most expensive meal of the trip but worth it
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat and hot chocolate at MBC or Himalaya Hotel — NPR 900–1,300

day_by_day.notes: MBC to ABC: approximately 4 km, 1.5–2 hours. This is the highlight of the entire trip. October weather is generally clear and stable — ideal conditions. Temperatures at ABC can drop to -5°C to -10°C even in October mornings. Wear all your layers. Do not linger too long if you feel unwell at altitude. The descent from ABC back to lower elevations is the best remedy for altitude sickness.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the descent from MBC (or Himalaya Hotel) back through the gorge, retracing the trail through Deurali, Hinku Cave, and Himalaya Hotel. The descent is faster but hard on the knees — use trekking poles. The familiar trail feels different going downhill with new perspectives
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue descending through Dovan and Bamboo, arriving back at Sinuwa or Chhomrong by mid-afternoon. The increasing warmth and lush vegetation as you lose altitude is a welcome change. Arrive at Chhomrong and enjoy a well-deserved rest
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the successful ABC trek with fellow trekkers in Chhomrong. Hot shower, clean clothes, and a proper meal feel like luxury after the high-altitude teahouses

meals.breakfast: Porridge and eggs at MBC or Himalaya Hotel
meals.lunch: Noodle soup and snacks at Bamboo teahouse
meals.dinner: Celebrate with a special dinner at Chhomrong — try apple crumble or chocolate cake for dessert — NPR 800–1,100

day_by_day.notes: Descent day: approximately 14–16 km, 6–7 hours. Knees take significant strain on long descents — take breaks, use poles, and step carefully on wet stones. You have now completed the core Annapurna Sanctuary trek. The next days will offer a more relaxed pace with cultural exploration on the return route.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda (1,780m) — a shorter, easier day. The trail descends through terraced fields and forest. Jhinu Danda is famous for its natural hot springs by the Modi Khola river
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon soaking in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda — a perfect remedy for tired trekking muscles. The springs are set beside the rushing river with mountain views. This is one of the most rewarding rest stops on the entire circuit
day_by_day.evening: Return up to Jhinu Danda village for the evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early night. The hot springs will leave you deeply relaxed and refreshed

meals.breakfast: Eggs and toast at Chhomrong teahouse
meals.lunch: Light lunch of spring rolls or sandwiches at a Jhinu Danda teahouse
meals.dinner: Dal Bhat and vegetable curry at Jhinu Danda guesthouse — NPR 600–800

day_by_day.notes: Chhomrong to Jhinu Danda: approximately 5 km, 2 hours. This is a deliberate rest and recovery day — do not rush. The hot springs cost approximately NPR 200–300 entry. Bring a towel and swimwear. This detour via Jhinu is highly recommended and adds minimal extra distance to the return route.

day_by_day.morning: Trek from Jhinu Danda back toward Nayapul via Ghandruk (1,940m) — the largest Gurung village in the Annapurna region. The trail climbs from Jhinu through forest and terraced fields with excellent views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhre
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Ghandruk and explore this beautifully preserved Gurung village. Visit the Gurung Museum to learn about the indigenous culture, traditional dress, and the famous Gurkha military heritage. Walk the stone-paved lanes and interact with local villagers
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight in Ghandruk — one of the most atmospheric villages on the trek. Enjoy cultural performances if available at the teahouse. The village has excellent views for sunset over the Annapurna range

meals.breakfast: Tibetan bread and honey at Jhinu Danda
meals.lunch: Garlic soup and fried rice at a teahouse en route to Ghandruk
meals.dinner: Traditional Gurung meal at a local teahouse in Ghandruk — try Gundruk (fermented leafy greens) soup — NPR 700–900

day_by_day.notes: Jhinu Danda to Ghandruk: approximately 7 km, 3–4 hours. Ghandruk is a culturally rich village and a highlight of the return journey. The Gurung Museum (ACAP-run) is excellent and free with your conservation area permit. This is the best place to buy authentic local crafts and souvenirs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Ghandruk — wake up for sunrise views of the Annapurna range from the village. Take a short walk to the upper viewpoint above Ghandruk for a last look at the peaks. Then begin the descent to Kimche and onward to Nayapul via Birethanti
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Nayapul and catch a local bus or jeep back to Pokhara (approximately 1.5–2 hours). Check back in to your Pokhara lakeside guesthouse, drop your pack, and take a long hot shower. Spend the afternoon at leisure — visit a spa for a traditional Nepali massage, browse the lakeside market, or simply relax by Phewa Lake
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Pokhara to mark the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary Trek. Enjoy a proper restaurant meal with a wider menu choice after days of teahouse food

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Ghandruk teahouse — eggs, toast, porridge, and coffee
meals.lunch: Quick dal bhat or sandwiches at Birethanti before the bus
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Caffe Concerto or Moondance Restaurant in Pokhara — try grilled chicken, continental dishes, or fresh lake fish with a cold Everest beer — NPR 1,200–1,800

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk to Nayapul: approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours. You have now completed the full Annapurna Sanctuary circuit. Total trekking distance approximately 110–120 km over 11 days. Get a massage this evening — your legs deserve it. Confirm your return transport to Kathmandu for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Pokhara — wake up for a last sunrise view of the Annapurna range from Lakeside or take a short walk to the Peace Pagoda for a final panoramic farewell to the mountains. Visit the Seti River Gorge viewpoint in central Pokhara — a dramatic natural wonder often overlooked by trekkers
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer back to Kathmandu by tourist bus (6–7 hours) or domestic flight (25 minutes). If time allows before departure, visit Thamel in Kathmandu for last-minute souvenir shopping — thangka paintings, singing bowls, pashmina scarves, and trekking gear at good prices. Visit Boudhanath Stupa or Pashupatinath Temple if arriving with sufficient time
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Nepal — enjoy a farewell dinner in Kathmandu's Thamel district. Reflect on the extraordinary 14-day journey through one of the world's most spectacular mountain regions

meals.breakfast: Final Nepali breakfast in Pokhara — sel roti (rice flour doughnuts) with yogurt and honey at a local café
meals.lunch: Meal on the bus or at a roadside stop en route to Kathmandu
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Thamel House Restaurant or Yin Yang Restaurant in Kathmandu — try a full traditional Nepali set dinner with cultural dance performance — NPR 1,500–2,500

day_by_day.notes: This is your final day — keep it flexible based on your onward flight time. If departing late or the following day, Kathmandu has excellent museums (National Museum, Natural History Museum) and the Durbar Squares are worth visiting. Keep some Nepali Rupees for airport departure tax and last-minute purchases. Reflect on an incredible 14 days in the Himalayas — you have trekked to Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130m, experienced authentic Gurung and Magar village culture, and witnessed some of the most spectacular mountain scenery on Earth.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Annapurna, Nepal Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Annapurna Sanctuary, Annapurna Conservation Area Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Kathmandu airport to your boutique stay in the Annapurna Conservation Area. En route, stop at a scenic viewpoint along the Prithvi Highway to stretch and take in the first Himalayan panoramas. Your personal guide will brief you on the 14-day journey ahead during the drive.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your boutique lodge, enjoy a welcome drink of warm spiced Nepali tea and locally sourced honey on your private terrace. Gentle orientation walk around the lodge grounds as the sun sets behind the Annapurna massif. Early rest to acclimatize.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light snack box provided during private transfer — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, and Nepali mountain water
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner at the lodge's signature restaurant: multi-course Nepali tasting menu featuring dal bhat with organic lentils, sautéed seasonal highland vegetables, slow-braised lamb sekuwa, and house-made mango lassi

day_by_day.notes: Ensure all trekking permits (ACAP and TIMS) are pre-arranged by your luxury operator. Hydrate well and avoid alcohol on arrival night for acclimatization. Lodge elevation is approximately 1,000–2,000 m depending on base location.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided nature walk through the lower Annapurna foothills — explore subtropical forest trails rich with rhododendron, oak, and bamboo. Birdwatching session with binoculars provided; look for Himalayan monal, laughingthrush, and sunbirds. Gentle pace to begin acclimatization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby traditional Gurung village with your personal cultural guide. Explore stone-paved lanes, observe local weaving and farming practices, and enjoy a private demonstration of traditional thangka painting at a local artisan's studio.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset yoga session on the lodge's panoramic deck led by a resident Himalayan yoga instructor. Star-gazing experience with a telescope set up by the lodge naturalist — the Annapurna skies offer exceptional clarity in October.

meals.breakfast: Lavish lodge breakfast: freshly baked sourdough, Himalayan honey, farm eggs cooked to order, seasonal fruit platter, and Nepali masala chai
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the trail — gourmet bento boxes with quinoa salad, smoked yak cheese, whole-grain wraps, and fresh-pressed apple juice from local orchards
meals.dinner: Chef's table dinner at the lodge featuring Gurung-inspired cuisine: nettle soup, pan-seared river trout with buckwheat, and house-churned yak butter dessert with cardamom

day_by_day.notes: October is peak autumn trekking season in Annapurna — expect clear skies, golden foliage, and excellent mountain views. Layers recommended as temperatures drop significantly after sunset at altitude.

day_by_day.morning: Acclimatization hike to a higher elevation viewpoint (approx. 2,500–3,000 m) with your private mountain guide. Witness the Annapurna range bathed in golden morning light — ideal photography opportunity. Practice mindful breathing techniques introduced by your guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge for a premium wellness recovery session: Himalayan hot stone massage and aromatherapy treatment at the lodge spa using locally sourced juniper and rhododendron essential oils.
day_by_day.evening: Private documentary screening in the lodge library on Annapurna's geological and cultural history, followed by a curated conversation with a local mountaineering expert over premium Nepali raksi (millet spirit) and artisan charcuterie board.

meals.breakfast: Energizing pre-hike breakfast: steel-cut oat porridge with Himalayan berries, protein-rich eggs, whole-grain toast, and ginger lemon tea
meals.lunch: Warm trail lunch at a scenic rest point — thermos of lentil soup, stuffed parathas, and Himalayan dark chocolate
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at the lodge: slow-roasted Annapurna lamb with rosemary jus, roasted root vegetables, and a locally inspired dessert of sel roti with honey cream

day_by_day.notes: Acclimatization is critical before ascending further. The afternoon spa session aids muscle recovery and reduces altitude-related fatigue. Drink at least 3–4 liters of water throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the classic Annapurna Sanctuary trek — Day 1 of ascent. Trek from base through dense rhododendron and bamboo forests on well-maintained luxury trail routes. Spot wildlife including Himalayan tahr, langur monkeys, and red pandas if fortunate. Private guide leads at a comfortable pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a mid-altitude premium teahouse camp or luxury tented camp (pre-arranged by operator). Afternoon free for journaling, photography, and soaking in the mountain atmosphere. Optional short exploratory walk around the camp perimeter.
day_by_day.evening: Campfire gathering under the stars with your guide sharing Annapurna folklore and mountaineering stories. Warm beverages and light snacks around the fire.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast before departure: eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit, and premium Darjeeling tea
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed at a panoramic trail rest stop — mezze-style spread with hummus, flatbread, dried fruits, nuts, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: Luxury teahouse/camp dinner: hearty Nepali thali with freshly made dal, seasonal vegetable curry, rice, pickles, and warm apple cider

day_by_day.notes: Trek distance today is approximately 10–14 km with gradual elevation gain. Porters carry all heavy luggage — you carry only a light daypack. Trekking poles highly recommended from this day forward.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning trek through the Modi Khola river valley — one of the most scenic corridors in the Himalayas. The trail narrows as you enter the dramatic gorge leading toward the Annapurna Sanctuary. Waterfalls, hanging bridges, and sheer cliff faces make this a spectacular morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a higher-altitude luxury camp. Rest and acclimatization period. Optional guided meditation session with views of Hiunchuli and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain) — one of Nepal's most sacred and iconic peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset photography walk with your guide to a curated viewpoint. Return to camp for a warm soak in a portable luxury foot bath set up by camp staff, followed by a gentle stretching session.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: fresh pancakes with honey and butter, boiled eggs, muesli, and ginger tea
meals.lunch: Trail lunch at a scenic waterfall rest point — warm soup from a thermos, energy bars, fresh fruit, and trail mix
meals.dinner: Camp dinner: pasta with slow-cooked tomato and herb sauce, garlic bread, mixed greens, and hot chocolate with Himalayan salt

day_by_day.notes: Elevation gain is significant today — maintain a slow, steady pace (pole-pole). Report any headaches or nausea to your guide immediately. The gorge section can be slippery after morning frost; waterproof boots essential.

day_by_day.morning: Final ascent into the Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) at approximately 4,130 m — a landmark achievement. The amphitheater of peaks including Annapurna I (8,091 m), Annapurna South, Hiunchuli, and Machhapuchhre surrounds you in a 360-degree panorama of raw Himalayan grandeur.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exploration of the ABC plateau with your guide. Learn about the history of Annapurna I — the first 8,000 m peak ever summited (1950, French expedition). Photography session in optimal afternoon light. Rest and warm up in your premium camp facility.
day_by_day.evening: Ceremonial arrival dinner at ABC — a special celebratory meal prepared by your private camp chef. Toast the achievement with a glass of premium Himalayan sparkling water (alcohol not recommended at this altitude) and exchange stories with fellow trekkers if any are present.

meals.breakfast: High-altitude energy breakfast: oatmeal with protein powder, dried fruits, peanut butter toast, and electrolyte tea
meals.lunch: Warm packed lunch at ABC upon arrival: noodle soup, crackers with yak cheese, energy gels, and hot lemon drink
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner: roasted vegetable and lentil stew, freshly baked flatbread, spiced potato curry, and a special dessert of warm brownie with condensed milk

day_by_day.notes: At 4,130 m, altitude sickness is a real risk. Move slowly, breathe deeply, and stay hydrated. Symptoms such as severe headache, vomiting, or confusion require immediate descent. Your guide carries emergency oxygen and a satellite communicator.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for the iconic ABC sunrise — arguably one of the most spectacular natural light shows on Earth as the first rays of sun ignite the Annapurna peaks in shades of gold, pink, and crimson. Private photography session with your guide at the best vantage points.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin descent from ABC toward a lower-altitude luxury camp, allowing the body to recover from peak altitude. The descent retraces through the stunning gorge with a fresh perspective and renewed energy. Notice details missed on the ascent.
day_by_day.evening: Arrival at lower-altitude camp — the body immediately feels the relief of richer oxygen. Hot shower (portable camp shower), a full body massage from a traveling spa therapist (pre-arranged luxury service), and relaxed evening around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at ABC: hot porridge, boiled eggs, toast with jam, and warm masala chai enjoyed with the most dramatic mountain backdrop on Earth
meals.lunch: Descent picnic at a scenic rest point — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and herbal tea
meals.dinner: Lower camp dinner: grilled chicken with roasted vegetables, rice pilaf, fresh cucumber salad, and warm apple crumble dessert

day_by_day.notes: Descent is physically easier but hard on knees — trekking poles essential. Take your time on steep sections. The emotional high of having reached ABC combined with physical fatigue can cause inattention; stay focused on the trail.

day_by_day.morning: Continue descent through the rhododendron forest zone — in October, the foliage turns rich amber and crimson. Birdwatching opportunities are excellent at this altitude band. A relaxed morning pace allows you to fully absorb the forest atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the base lodge or a premium teahouse village. Hot shower, laundry service (arranged by lodge), and free time to explore the village market for handcrafted souvenirs — Gurung jewelry, hand-woven textiles, and Tibetan singing bowls.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Gurung cultural performance arranged privately at the lodge — folk music, dance, and storytelling by local performers. Intimate and authentic experience curated exclusively for your group.

meals.breakfast: Camp breakfast: French press coffee, granola with yogurt, banana pancakes, and fresh orange juice
meals.lunch: Village teahouse lunch: dal bhat with all accompaniments — the classic Nepali trekker's meal, freshly prepared and endlessly refillable
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: four-course meal — amuse-bouche of spiced pumpkin soup, mixed greens salad with yak cheese, main of slow-braised pork belly with seasonal vegetables, and cardamom crème brûlée

day_by_day.notes: This is a significant recovery day. Treat any blisters or muscle soreness with the lodge's first-aid and wellness resources. Celebrate the completion of the Annapurna Sanctuary trek — a world-class achievement.

day_by_day.morning: Guided nature hike on a lesser-known trail branching off the main circuit — explore hidden waterfalls, local shrines, and pristine forest untouched by mass tourism. Your expert naturalist guide identifies medicinal plants used in traditional Ayurvedic and Tibetan medicine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm and participate in a premium farm-to-table cooking class — learn to prepare authentic Nepali dishes including momos (dumplings), dal bhat, and aloo tama (bamboo shoot and potato curry) under the guidance of a professional Nepali chef.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the fruits of your culinary labor at a private dining setup on the lodge terrace with views of the illuminated Annapurna range under a full October moon. Sommelier-paired non-alcoholic Himalayan botanical drinks accompany each course.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: avocado toast on sourdough, poached eggs, smoked salmon, fresh fruit bowl, and ginger-turmeric latte
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the organic farm: fresh salad with farm vegetables, homemade bread, and herbal infusions
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner featuring dishes prepared in your cooking class, elevated by the lodge chef with premium plating and presentation

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class is a highlight for food-loving travelers and provides an authentic cultural exchange. Dietary preferences and allergies should be communicated to the lodge in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day exploration of the Annapurna Conservation Area's biodiversity — morning game walk with a wildlife specialist tracking signs of snow leopard, Himalayan wolf, and musk deer. Even if large mammals remain elusive, the birdlife and flora are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) headquarters or a local conservation center to learn about the groundbreaking conservation model that protects this UNESCO-recognized landscape. Meet a local ranger or conservation officer for an insider briefing.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing astronomy session with a professional guide using high-powered telescopes — the Annapurna region is one of Asia's premier dark-sky destinations. Identify constellations, planets, and the Milky Way core in stunning clarity.

meals.breakfast: Early morning energizing breakfast: muesli with Himalayan berries, boiled eggs, whole-grain toast, and Nepali black tea
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch in the field: artisan wraps, roasted vegetable salad, premium trail mix, and cold-pressed juice
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner: Tibetan-inspired hot pot with yak broth, fresh vegetables, noodles, and dipping sauces, followed by butter tea ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Bring warm layers for the evening stargazing session — temperatures at this altitude drop sharply after dark in October. The wildlife walk requires patience and silence; follow your guide's instructions closely.

day_by_day.morning: Helicopter scenic flight over the Annapurna massif — a truly once-in-a-lifetime luxury experience offering aerial perspectives of Annapurna I, Dhaulagiri, Machhapuchhre, and the entire sanctuary from above. Land at a high-altitude viewpoint for a brief walk and photography session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the lodge and enjoy a full afternoon at the luxury spa — choose from a menu of treatments including a Himalayan salt scrub, deep tissue mountain massage, and a traditional Ayurvedic shirodhara (warm oil head treatment).
day_by_day.evening: Private chef's tasting dinner at the lodge — a seven-course culinary journey through Nepal's diverse regional cuisines, from the Terai lowlands to the high Himalayas, paired with premium non-alcoholic botanical cocktails crafted from local herbs and flowers.

meals.breakfast: Pre-flight light breakfast: fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, granola, and green tea
meals.lunch: Post-helicopter celebration lunch at the lodge: wood-fired pizza with Nepali toppings (yak cheese, local herbs), fresh salad, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Seven-course chef's tasting menu — a gastronomic highlight of the trip featuring rare local ingredients and innovative Nepali-fusion cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flights are subject to weather conditions — your operator will have a contingency plan (alternative scenic viewpoint hike) if weather prevents flying. Book helicopter slots well in advance as demand is high in October.

day_by_day.morning: Guided meditation and mindfulness retreat morning at the lodge — a certified Himalayan meditation teacher leads a three-hour immersive session combining breathwork, sound healing with Tibetan singing bowls, and guided visualization using the mountain landscape as a backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearby Ghandruk village — one of the most picturesque Gurung villages in the Annapurna region. Walk its stone-paved streets, visit the Gurung Museum, and interact with local families in a respectful, guide-facilitated cultural exchange.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell bonfire at the lodge with your guide team — an evening of gratitude, storytelling, and traditional Nepali music. Exchange gifts with your guide and porter team in the Nepali tradition of acknowledging those who made the journey possible.

meals.breakfast: Mindful breakfast: warm congee with ginger and scallions, steamed buns, fresh fruit, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Ghandruk village lunch at a premium local restaurant: authentic Gurung cuisine including gundruk soup, dhido (buckwheat porridge), and local vegetables
meals.dinner: Farewell lodge dinner: whole roasted chicken with herb jus, roasted Himalayan potatoes, seasonal greens, and a decadent chocolate fondant with local honey ice cream

day_by_day.notes: Ghandruk is approximately 1–2 hours from most Annapurna base lodges. The village is one of the best-preserved examples of Gurung culture and is highly recommended for cultural immersion.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise hike to a nearby panoramic viewpoint — a reflective morning walk to absorb the last views of the Annapurna range before departure. Bring your journal, camera, and a thermos of tea. A moment for quiet gratitude and reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout from the boutique lodge. Private luxury vehicle transfer back toward Kathmandu or Pokhara (depending on departure logistics). En route, stop in Pokhara for a lakeside lunch and exploration of the charming lakeside promenade along Phewa Lake.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium Pokhara hotel (e.g., Tiger Mountain Pokhara Lodge or similar luxury property). Relaxed evening stroll along Lakeside with views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges reflected in Phewa Lake at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Final lodge breakfast: full spread of eggs, pastries, fruit, granola, and your choice of hot beverage — savor every bite
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch in Pokhara at a premium restaurant: grilled lake fish, fresh salad, and cold-pressed juice with a view of Phewa Lake and the mountains
meals.dinner: Dinner at one of Pokhara's finest restaurants: continental and Nepali fusion menu, rooftop setting with mountain views, and a celebratory mocktail toast to the journey

day_by_day.notes: Pokhara is the gateway city to the Annapurna region and worth exploring even briefly. The city sits at approximately 820 m — the drop in altitude from the mountains will feel like a warm embrace.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nepal — sunrise boat ride on Phewa Lake with a private guide, paddling toward the Tal Barahi Temple on the island. The reflection of the Annapurna range on the still morning lake is one of Nepal's most iconic and serene images.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Pokhara Regional Airport for a scenic 25-minute mountain flight to Kathmandu (or private helicopter transfer for the ultimate luxury finale). In Kathmandu, time permitting, visit Pashupatinath Temple or Boudhanath Stupa for a final cultural immersion before international departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tribhuvan International Airport, Kathmandu. Your luxury operator ensures VIP airport assistance, fast-track check-in, and lounge access. Depart with a heart full of Himalayan memories, a body rejuvenated by mountain air, and a deep connection to one of Earth's most extraordinary places.

meals.breakfast: Pokhara hotel breakfast: continental spread with fresh pastries, eggs, fruit, and premium coffee — enjoy at leisure before the lake excursion
meals.lunch: Kathmandu airport or city lunch: premium Nepali restaurant near Thamel — last taste of momos, dal bhat, and masala chai
meals.dinner: In-flight or at international transit lounge

day_by_day.notes: Allow sufficient time for Kathmandu traffic when planning airport transfers — the city can be congested, especially in the afternoon. Your luxury operator will have pre-calculated transfer times. Ensure all souvenirs comply with customs regulations — natural items (feathers, certain plants, antiques) may require documentation.

query: Nepal trekking Annapurna, $2000 solo, October 2026, 14 days
